prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
competitors_mentioned: Require a Manual J Load Calculation
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC contractor for everyone — the right company depends on your exact location in the Atlanta metro area, budget, the size/age of your home, brand preference, and whether you value lowest price vs. longest warranty or highest-efficiency equipment. I can, however, help you find a very good one and give you a checklist to make the choice confidently.

Quick local options to consider (examples that commonly serve Atlanta):
- Coolray (Coolray & Mr. Plumber) — large regional provider with strong local presence  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning — national brand with local techs and financing options  
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local franchise) — fast-response brand with nationwide backing  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter — offers HVAC plus plumbing/duct services

(These are examples — vet each for your ZIP and current reviews before hiring.)

How to pick the best contractor for your AC replacement
1. Get at least 3 written quotes and compare apples-to-apples (same capacity, SEER rating, brand, warranty, and scope of work).  
2. Verify license and insurance — make sure the tech/company is licensed to install HVAC in Georgia and carries liability insurance and workers’ comp. Ask for license numbers and verify online.  
3. Ask about qualifications — NATE-certified technicians, factory training for the brand you want, and years of experience with full-system installs.  
4. Require a Manual J load calculation and proper equipment sizing — a good company won’t just match your old unit’s tonnage.  
5. Check warranty details — parts and labor, length of manufacturer warranty, and whether the installer provides a performance/installation warranty.  
6. Read recent reviews — Google, Yelp, and BBB; ask for recent references in your neighborhood.  
7. Confirm permits and inspections — responsible contractors pull required permits and coordinate inspections.  
8. Ask about removal of old unit, ductwork evaluation/repairs, refrigerant handling, timeline, and cleanup.  
9. Watch out for very low bids — they often hide costs or cut corners on installation or equipment.  
10. Get financing/options in writing if you need it.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? Can I see your license number?  
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and show me the results?  
- Which brand and model do you recommend and why? What SEER rating?  
- What is included in the price (permit, labor, materials, removal of old unit, duct modifications)?  
- What are the manufacturer and installer warranties? Are labor warranties transferable?  
- Do your technicians have NATE or factory training?  
- When can you start and how long will installation take?

If you’d like, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies near your address or ZIP code, or  
- Draft an email/template to send to contractors when requesting quotes, or  
- Help you compare 2–3 written estimates you receive.

Tell me your ZIP code and any brand or budget preferences and I’ll find 3–5 highly rated installers in your area.
